name: Rhetorical Question Density
description: Analyzes the frequency and structural placement of question marks within a text. Large Language Models frequently rely on rhetorical questions as a lazy transitional device to move between paragraphs or to simulate conversational engagement (e.g., 'But what does this mean for the future?', 'How can we solve this?'). This results in an artificially high density of question marks used purely for structural scaffolding rather than genuine inquiry.
mechanism: The algorithm isolates all interrogative punctuation (question marks) and maps their position relative to paragraph boundaries. It calculates the overall 'Question Mark Density' (questions per 1000 words) and a 'Transitional Interrogative Score' (how often questions appear exactly at the end of an introductory paragraph or the beginning of a body paragraph). AI models, trained to be highly explanatory and structured, use questions as a reliable heuristic to introduce the next topic without requiring complex narrative transitions. Human writers use rhetorical questions much more sparingly, relying on natural semantic flow to transition between ideas.
useCase: Highly effective for auditing blog posts, marketing content, and explanatory essays where the AI's tendency to use the 'Question-Then-Answer' format becomes glaringly repetitive.
strengths:
• Easily identifies the classic 'AI essay structure' which almost always features a transitional question before the conclusion.
• Requires minimal computational power, as it relies on punctuation mapping rather than deep semantic parsing.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives in FAQ (Frequently Asked Questions) documents, interviews, or genuine conversational transcripts where high question density is expected.
• Less effective on extremely short texts or highly technical documentation where rhetorical questions are naturally absent.
parameters:
Analysis: Punctuation Extraction and Positional Mapping
Metric: Question Marks per 1000 Words & Paragraph-Boundary Proximity
Output: 0-100 Interrogative Predictability (Artificial Transition) Score
accuracy: Moderate — 70-80% accuracy in explanatory and blog-style texts. Weak standalone metric but powerful when combined with 'Paragraph Structure' analysis.

references.title: Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
Fagni, T. et al. (2021). TweepFake: About detecting deepfake tweets. PLOS ONE.
